newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan share prices end higher in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan share prices end higher in listless trade.

text.p: Taiwan stocks finished Tuesday's listless session higher but turnover shrank amid annual selling linked to Friday's Mid-Autumn festival, brokers said.
Initial buying triggered by the government's decision to raise its ceiling for combined foreign investment in the domestic stock market failed to gather momentum, brokers said.
"This is good news but we may have to wait for a while until foreign funds actually enter Taiwan," said Wang Jieh of Foremost Investment Services.
The weighted index gained 23.87 points or 0.37 percent to end at 6,477.85. Turnover was a modest T$33 billion.

The central bank and finance ministry will raise the foreign fund ceiling to 25 percent from 20 percent in any listed firm and the overall market by end-1996, and some brokers speculate the liberalisation could take effect as soon as October.

They also noted continued selling from many firms to raise cash to pay bonuses or buy gifts for employees and clients for Friday's Mid-Autumn festival, a major Taiwan holiday that will close the island's financial markets for two days.
"I don't worry about the recent slow sentiment because investors are always conservative at high levels," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming.
The electronics sector led the gains due to their sound fundamentals and hopes for a new influx of investment by foreign interests, brokers said.
Semiconductor manufacturer Mosel was the most actively traded issue, gaining 50 cents or 1.44 percent to T$35.3. Electronic appliance maker Tatung Co surged T$2.1 or 4.29 percent to T$51.
Brokers expected share prices to hold to current levels and the index to move around 6,500 points in the near term, with sentiment remaining positive.
